messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up to the private endpoint/NAT fallback RFC. I sketched an alternative that uses a tokenized ephemeral relay for outbound egress when a customer VPC can't/shouldn't use our standard private endpoint path. Main ask: feedback on token lifetime, rotation, revocation, and operational cost. cc @Maria @Kevin

Maria: Interesting. Short version: token is fine, but avoid a central revocation DB at scale. Prefer short-lived tokens + occasional revocation list with GC. :+1:

Kevin: From SRE POV two immediate concerns: token issuance bursts during connector restarts, and mapping tokens -> ENI/NAT resources. We need rate limits + issuance metrics. Also how do we fail open/closed if tokens run out?

Alex: Good call. Failback plan idea: if token service is saturated, connectors fall back to "global egress pool" (lower priority, higher cost) with clear telemetry so we can alert customers. That keeps apps online.

Jordan: Architecturally, allocating an ENI per token is too heavy. We should pool ENIs and maintain ephemeral SNAT mappings: token -> 5-tuple mapping on the NAT gateway. That lets us reuse IPs but preserve per-connector attribution for logging.

Chris: Security notes: tokens must be bound to connector identity + intended audience + short nonce. Sign with KMS. Two options for revocation: 1) very short TTL (e.g., 5m) so revocation almost never needed; 2) short TTL + revocation list for abuse cases. Also require mTLS on the connector side to avoid token theft.

Alex: Proposal sketch: issuance flow:

```
POST /v1/relays/token -> authenticated connector bootstrap
Response: { token, expires_at, assigned_pool_id }
```

Token payload: [connector_id, pool_id, nonce, iat, exp], signed by CP KMS. Token used in relay handshake. Token TTL default = 5m, configurable per-account with guardrails.

Maria: If TTL = 5m we need clock skew tolerance and a simple refresh endpoint so connectors can prefetch. Also add a token use counter in logs for debugging.

Kevin: Operational playbook items:
- rate-limit per-account token issuance (e.g., 100/min)
- emit metrics: token_issued, token_failed, token_reused, pool_exhaustion
- alert on pool_exhaustion and sustained issuance spikes

Jordan: For SNAT mapping semantics: pool_id -> set of IPs, maintain ephemeral mapping table with TTL = token.exp. When a token present, we pin mapping for that token duration. After expiry, mapping can be reclaimed. Need eviction policy for sticky sessions (long-lived) vs churn.

Chris: Audit: write every issuance event to CP audit stream immediately (append-only). That gives us forensics if a token is misused. Also add a second check: token audience must include the exact destination service type (e.g., outbound:egress-rely) to avoid token reuse across different flows.

Alex: Two operational questions I couldn't decide on: 1) default TTL (5m vs 15m). 2) whether to support a long-lived bootstrap token for offline connectors that can't rotate frequently. Thoughts?

Maria: Default 5m. For offline connectors, one-time bootstrap token (long-lived) that can exchange for ephemeral tokens when online. But bootstrap tokens must be rate-limited and auditable.

Kevin: Agree on 5m. For bootstrap tokens, add explicit admin actions to revoke and require MFA for issuance. Also track token churn per-account to detect automation loops.

Jordan: Implementation note: try to keep the mapping table in-memory in the regional relay plane with eventual persistence for crash recovery. Avoid a hard dependency on a single DB for low-latency lookups.

Chris: Also encryption-in-flight/on-rest must be explicit: tokens never appear in logs (only token_id). Use token_id->event mapping for audits.

relay-bot: Token issuance service deployed to staging/region-3 at 2026-03-23T15:22:04Z :rocket:

Alex: Thanks all — this is helpful. Action items: I'll update RFC with a token flow diagram, default TTL=5m, bootstrap-token model, and a spike to measure ENI/SNAT pool scaling. Kevin/Maria/Jordan/Chris — please add any blocking concerns as comments on the RFC. I'll aim to post the RFC update tomorrow. :thumbsup:
